mon long-term effects of these drugs, although it is often diffi-
cult to distinguish these effects from the complications of the 
disease itself (see Chapter 36). Serotonin antagonists such as 
ondansetron (Zofran) help to reduce these GI side effects, 
which decrease activity of the chemoreceptor trigger zone in the 
brain, thus reducing nausea and vomiting.
Drugs can cause changes in bowel function that can lead to 
constipation or diarrhea. Narcotic agents such as codeine and 
morphine cause a nonproductive increase in smooth muscle 
tone of the intestinal muscle wall, thereby decreasing peristalsis 
and causing constipation. Methylnaltrexone (Relistor) is a laxa-
tive, administered subcutaneously, and specifically indicated for 
severe opioid-induced constipation.

by decreasing intestinal secretions, slowing peristalsis, and 
causing constipation. The atypical antipsychotics, tricyclic anti-
